newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ruggiero hopes China will hasten WTO negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Ruggiero hopes China will hasten WTO negotiations.

text.p: The director-general of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Renato Ruggiero, on Wednesday expressed the hope that Chinese leaders will show a strong political commitment to quicken negotiations on China's membership of the body, a Japanese government official said.
Ruggiero expressed the hope during a meeting with Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato, the ministry official said.
Ruggiero, who is to visit China in April, was quoted as saying that it is important to take into account political aspects of the issue of China's membership.

The ministry official paraphrased Ruggiero's comments as meaning that he wants Chinese leaders to send a political message to Chinese negotiators to speed up negotiations despite apparent reluctance among some groups in China regarding its membership in the world trade body.
Sato told Ruggiero that through various contacts he knew that China had high hopes on Ruggiero's visit in mid-April.
Ruggiero was quoted as saying he would like the WTO to hold a 50th anniversary event in the first half of 1998 to mark the founding of its predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.

The Japanese official said there was a consensus in the WTO that the anniversary event should be held in 1998, but opinions still varied as to who should attend the event, to be held in Geneva, where the group is based.
Sato was quoted as saying that both rich and poor nations should participate in the event.
"It is important that a decision on who should attend the event be made after thorough discussions between the rich and poor nations," Sato said.
